findings.title: Both retrieval and generation are underperforming
findings.detail: Faithfulness (0.143) and Context Recall (0.167) are both below 0.7. This indicates retrieval is missing key information AND generation is hallucinating with what it has.
suggested_actions: Focus on retrieval FIRST — generation cannot improve until context is correct
Increase top-K or add hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vector)
Re-evaluate after retrieval fix, then revisit generation

findings.title: Hit@5 is low — coverage problem
findings.detail: Hit@5 = 0.667. The retrieval often fails to return any relevant chunk in top-5.
suggested_actions: Switch to a stronger embedding model

findings.title: Precision@5 is low — noise problem
findings.detail: Precision@5 = 0.200. Too many irrelevant chunks are in top-5, which can confuse the LLM.
suggested_actions: Add a re-ranker to push noise down
Raise similarity threshold (filter out low-score chunks)

findings.title: Answer Relevancy is low — answers are off-topic or unfocused
findings.detail: Answer Relevancy = 0.566. The LLM is producing answers that drift from the question or include tangential content.
suggested_actions: Add explicit prompt instruction: 'Answer ONLY the question asked, no tangents'
Lower maxOutputTokens to constrain answer length
Add few-shot examples of focused answers

findings.title: Context Precision is low — LLM is processing too much noise
findings.detail: Context Precision = 0.333. The retrieved chunks include many that aren't needed to answer the question. This can degrade generation quality even when the right information IS present.
suggested_actions: Add a re-ranker to filter chunks before sending to the LLM

per_question.question: What was the nickname of Niels Jorgensen's fire company that he heard over the radio on 9/11?
What bug caused Stanley, the Stanford autonomous car, to fail every 30 miles during DARPA Grand Challenge development?
per_question.answer: Stanley, the car that eventually won the DARPA Grand Challenge, would commit suicide every 30 miles due to a bug where the sinking of two computer clocks occasionally caused a clock to go backwards. This negative time elapsed screwed up the entire internal logic, and it took a long time to find this bug [Source 1].

per_question.question: How does Richard Dawkins distinguish between the two modes of meme transmission, and what does he compare each one to?
per_question.answer: Richard Dawkins distinguishes between two modes of meme transmission. One mode is longitudinal, from grandparent to parent to child, which he compares to conventional genetic transmission [Source 2]. The other mode is transverse, which he compares to viral transmission, as seen when a charismatic preacher converts people [Source 1].
